I'll draw it as SVG and render with rsvg-convert.

I made a turtle and saved it to ~/Desktop/turtle.png. It's 1024 by 1024. It's a green cartoon turtle walking right, with a dome shell, a small smile and pink cheeks, on a soft sky-to-sand gradient. I opened the file to check it renders. The source SVG is at /tmp/turtle.svg if you want changes.

make it walk in an animated svg now

The walking turtle is at ~/Desktop/turtle-walk.svg. Open it in a browser to watch it.

It walks in place while the grass tufts on the ground slide left, so it looks like it's moving forward. The legs step in diagonal pairs, the way a real turtle walks. The shell bobs with each step, the head nods, the tail wags and the grapes wobble on top. The loop is 1.2 seconds.

I took headless Chrome screenshots at two moments, and the legs and ground were in different places, so the animation runs. The motion is plain CSS inside the SVG. It plays in browsers. Image viewers like Preview may only show a still frame.

I found the preview card. It's the Slab menu bar's LocalArtifactPreview. Now I'm checking what else reads it before I add SVG.
Now tests for both sides.
The Swift probe was already broken before my change. It doesn't pull in SoundSketch. I'll add that file to it.
The probe passes. Now I'm building the menu bar to make sure it compiles.
It compiles. Next I'll load the turtle SVG into a real WKWebView, using the card's own HTML and CSP, and snapshot it twice to check it moves.

Animated SVGs now show on the Aesel TUI's preview card, and they move. I haven't installed the new menu bar build, so your running copy won't show them until you rebuild and reinstall it.

The card is drawn by the Slab menu bar. The TUI only tells it which file to show. So most of the change is on the Slab side:

- **Aesel:** `aesel/src/media.mjs` now treats `.svg` as a picture. An SVG a tool writes, or one you pin with `/preview`, goes to the card.
- **Card:** `LocalArtifactPreview.swift` accepts `image/svg+xml`. The SVG is copied into the card's folder as `artifact.svg`. WebKit only draws an SVG when it has its extension, so without the rename it stays blank. The card gets its size from the SVG's width and height, or from its viewBox if those are missing.
- **Loading:** `PromptPreview.swift` used to reject anything macOS's image loader couldn't open, and that loader can't read SVG. Now an SVG just has to be text with an `<svg>` tag.

The SVG loads as a plain image. Its CSS and SMIL animations play, but its scripts don't run and it can't fetch anything. That matches how the card already treats project files.

To check it, I put turtle-walk.svg into a real WKWebView using the card's own page and security settings. It loaded and fired the card's ready signal. I took two snapshots 0.45 seconds apart and 12% of the pixels changed: the legs stepped, the head nodded and the grass moved.

The menu bar package builds. The card's test script was already broken before I touched it, because it was missing one Swift file. I fixed that and added SVG cases, and it passes. The Aesel media tests pass too.

Nothing is committed. `media.mjs` already had someone else's uncommitted edits in it, so only one of its changed lines is mine.
